moments.title: The founding of Archelaos by physical education inspector Georgios Efthymiou on 29 April
paragraphs: On 29 April 1956, the founding statutes of G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis were drawn up at the initiative of Pieria's physical education inspector, Georgios Efthymiou (1908–2006). Athanasios Tsaknakis, Ioannis Zarogiannis and Theodoros Xiromeritis also served on the first founding board. Inspired by the ancient Macedonian king Archelaus I, they laid the foundations of organised athletics in Pieria.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Official judicial recognition of the club in 1957
paragraphs: The new association received official legal recognition from the Court of First Instance of Katerini under Decision 38/1957 and was entered in the register of recognised associations as no. 2/1957. This established Archelaos as an autonomous institution and one of Pieria's longest-standing active athletics organisations.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The Prefecture of Pieria entrusts the Dia Games to Archelaos
paragraphs: By Decision 4060 of 18 March 1957, the acting Prefect of Pieria, Menelaos Tsakiris, entrusted Archelaos with organising the annual Dia athletics games. The purpose was to revive the ancient Macedonian games traditionally associated with King Archelaus and the sanctuary of Zeus at Dion.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The first Dia Games take place in Katerini's Municipal Park
paragraphs: On 30 June 1957, the first official Dia athletics games took place at Katerini's Municipal Park under the club's auspices and the presidency of Athanasios Tsaknakis. Despite limited facilities, the event attracted local interest and laid the foundations for a long-running athletics tradition in Pieria.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The presidency of Theofilos Kamperidis and the club's ties with Katerini
paragraphs: Theofilos Kamperidis, later mayor of Katerini and a member of parliament for Pieria, presided over the club from 1959 to 1961, succeeding Ioannis Mantzaropoulos. During his tenure Archelaos strengthened its links with local institutions, and the second Dia Games were held in the Municipal Park.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Takis Paraskevopoulos begins a long coaching era in athletics
paragraphs: In 1964 Dimitrios (Takis) Paraskevopoulos became the club's athletics coach while continuing to compete in throwing events. His service lasted more than three decades, until June 1996, and was instrumental in developing athletes who went on to earn national, Balkan and Olympic distinctions.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The women's track and field team finishes fifth nationally
paragraphs: In 1966, less than a decade after the club's creation, the Archelaos women's athletics team finished fifth overall at the Greek Women's National Championships. This was an early major team distinction and helped establish Katerini on the national athletics map.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Official registration of Archelaos with SEGAS
paragraphs: On 20 May 1967, during Ioannis Mantzaropoulos's presidency, Archelaos was officially registered with SEGAS, the Greek athletics federation, under membership number 238. Registration opened the way for the club's athletes to participate fully in national championship competitions.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Green and yellow are established as the club's colours
paragraphs: The board minutes of 27 June 1968 record the official adoption of green and yellow (gold) as the club's colours, with white as an alternative kit. The same year saw the successful revival of the fourth Dia Games, further establishing Archelaos's identity.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Archelaos preserves its independence by rejecting a proposed merger
paragraphs: In January 1970, S.F.K. Pierikos submitted a written merger proposal (protocol 261 of 14 January). At meetings on 22 and 26 January, the board led by Ioannis Mantzaropoulos unanimously rejected the proposal, preserving the independence and historical continuity of Archelaos.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Alkinoos Tasopoulos sets a club record in the 3,000-metre steeplechase
paragraphs: As a young steeplechase runner in 1971, Alkinoos (Alkis) Tasopoulos finished second at the Greek Junior Championships and recorded 9:42.2 over 3,000 metres steeplechase. The performance became a long-standing club record. He later served as president of Archelaos from 2019 to 2026.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Physical education teachers usher in a new multi-sport era
paragraphs: On 24 June 1973, five physical education teachers—Athanasios Efthymiou, Dimitrios Paraskevopoulos, Efstathios Zannas, Orestis Ntarlagiannis and Theodoros Sfikas—took over the club's administration. They inherited its records in a military chest, established permanent offices at the Papageorgiou building and began transforming Archelaos into a multi-sport organisation.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The basketball department is founded
paragraphs: At the meeting of 26 June 1973, the board decided to establish a basketball department, with Theodoros Sfikas taking organisational and coaching responsibility. Following recognition by the Greek basketball federation, the team played early friendly matches in 1974, including against Filippos Verias, and entered regional men's and women's competitions that April.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The volleyball department is founded
paragraphs: The volleyball department was set up alongside basketball in the summer of 1973 and registered with the Greek volleyball federation. Orestis Ntarlagiannis and Christos Eleftheroudis were early team officials, while Theodoros Sfikas and Avraam Terzopoulos coached the side as official competition began in 1974.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The club navigates the mobilisation during the Cyprus crisis
paragraphs: During the mobilisation following the Turkish invasion of Cyprus in July and August 1974, the club temporarily suspended sporting activity. Board records dated 6 August and 13 September document the administration's efforts, under Athanasios Efthymiou, to keep its teams together and safely resume training.
The museum chronology also records summer swimming training at the seaside during this period.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The fifth Dia Games bring clubs from across Greece to Katerini
paragraphs: On 22–23 June 1974, following a six-year hiatus, Archelaos revived the fifth Dia athletics games at Katerini's National Stadium, drawing 16 clubs from across Greece. The event became an annual national-level meeting under the authorisation of SEGAS.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The artistic gymnastics department is established
paragraphs: On 3 April 1975, during the presidency of Nikos Tsinopoulos, the board established the artistic gymnastics department. Physical education teacher Stavros Diamantopoulos volunteered as its first coach, with Orestis Ntarlagiannis as team official, making Archelaos one of the pioneering regional clubs in the sport.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Archelaos enters the national artistic gymnastics championships
paragraphs: In May 1975, only one month after the department was founded, young Archelaos gymnasts made their first appearance at the Greek National Artistic Gymnastics Championships in Thessaloniki, as recorded in the board minutes of 13 May. This marked the beginning of the club's later national success in gymnastics.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: A landmark volleyball friendly against Panathinaikos
paragraphs: To promote volleyball among young people in Pieria, Archelaos organised a friendly match against Panathinaikos in 1975. Played in the open courtyard of Katerini's Boys' Gymnasium, now the 5th Gymnasium, it attracted local spectators and students.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The constitution is updated while the club retains its autonomy
paragraphs: On 28 June 1976, Archelaos amended its statutes to comply with Sports Law 75/1975; the amendment was approved by Katerini's Court of First Instance under Decision 121/1976. The board also defended the club's policy on the release of key athletes to other associations that September.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The decision to establish a handball department
paragraphs: Following a proposal by Efstathios Zannas, the board voted on 22 December 1976 to establish a handball department. The decision introduced a new Olympic sport to Pieria, which would eventually bring Archelaos major national titles and appearances in European competitions.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The table tennis department is created
paragraphs: At the same board meeting on 22 December 1976, the club decided to establish a table tennis department. It joined the national table tennis federation in 1978, with Lazaros Blatzas as its first team official and Ntinokas and Lytras on its technical committee.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Katerini's new indoor sports hall opens
paragraphs: The indoor gymnasium of Katerini's National Sports Centre was officially inaugurated on 12 September 1977. Now known as the Second Municipal Sports Centre, it provided a home for handball, basketball, volleyball, gymnastics and wrestling, which had previously relied largely on outdoor facilities.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Archelaos hosts a national youth artistic gymnastics championship
paragraphs: In October 1977, SEGAS entrusted Archelaos with organising the first Greek Junior Boys' and Girls' Artistic Gymnastics Championships. The competition was hosted in the newly built indoor sports hall in Katerini, recognising the club's progress and organisational capabilities.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The men's basketball team reaches the second national division
paragraphs: Four years after its creation, Archelaos's men's basketball team won promotion to Greece's Second National Division for 1977–78, relying on locally developed players including Konstantinos Tsougranis and Tsagkalidis. The team competed in the division for two consecutive seasons, from 1977 to 1979.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Dimitrios Giannaros becomes club president
paragraphs: On 20 December 1977, following Nikos Tsinopoulos's resignation for health reasons, Dimitrios (Mitsos) Giannaros was elected club president. During his eight-year tenure, six new sporting departments were founded, the board expanded to 15 members and the club celebrated its 25th anniversary in 1981.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Ioannis Ziogas helps form the handball team
paragraphs: In January 1978, the handball department completed its organisation, with Christos Papakonstantinou as its first team official; on 9 March, Ioannis Ziogas was hired as its first coach. In May, Archelaos held an official handball-promotion tournament in Katerini, recorded in the minutes of 16 May 1978.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Freestyle and Greco-Roman wrestling join the club
paragraphs: On 4 April 1978, Lazaros Tsakiridis and Lazaros Psomiadis submitted a proposal to the board to create freestyle and Greco-Roman wrestling departments. This laid the foundations for a team that would later achieve world, European and Mediterranean honours.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: A pioneering general gymnastics programme for young children
paragraphs: In February 1978, the club opened a general physical education programme for young children. Organised by Efstathios Zannas, with Penelope Zourna and Veta Zouka as its first instructors, it operated until 1983 and introduced hundreds of children to sport before they entered competitive departments.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Zaira Lazaridou sets a national junior discus record
paragraphs: In May 1978, according to the board minutes of 9 May, Archelaos thrower Zaira Lazaridou set a Greek junior women's discus record of 43.80 metres. She later threw 14.51 metres in the shot put in 1981, represented the national team and served as an athletics coach at the club from 1985 to 1990.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Archelaos helps found the Hellenic Handball Federation
paragraphs: In 1979, Archelaos was among the founding members of the independent Hellenic Handball Federation. With Charalambos Ioannidis as team official and Antonios Matthaiidis and Apostolos Pipilis as coaches, the department entered official federation championships, as recorded in the minutes of 27 November.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: An indoor air-rifle shooting range begins operating
paragraphs: The indoor airgun shooting range at Katerini's National Sports Centre was completed in 1979. Its construction prompted the creation of Archelaos's shooting department, which would go on to establish a strong position in Greek target shooting.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Official recognition for the wrestling department
paragraphs: Regular wrestling training began on 1 January 1980 under Lazaros Psomiadis, and the department received official federation recognition on 25 January. Dionysios Efthymiadis became the first team official in September, with Alekos Karypidis taking over as coach.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Archelaos helps establish the regional basketball association
paragraphs: In 1980, Archelaos was one of 11 founding clubs of the Central-Western Macedonia Basketball Clubs Association, the predecessor of EKASKEM. This step gave the region's basketball community an independent administrative structure.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: A formal decision to establish competitive swimming
paragraphs: On 14 October 1980, the board officially established a swimming department, along with a weightlifting department. Efstathios Zannas was appointed to organise swimming ahead of the opening of the municipal pool at Katerini's National Sports Centre.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Antonis Papadimitriou sets a national youth javelin record
paragraphs: At the tenth Dia athletics meeting, held on 11–12 October 1980, 17-year-old Archelaos javelin thrower Antonis Papadimitriou set a Greek boys' record of 63.02 metres. Further marks followed: 71.14 metres in 1981, 83.56 metres at Malmö in 1984 and a senior Greek record of 79.56 metres in 1987.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Official recognition for the shooting department
paragraphs: On 10 April 1981, Archelaos officially joined the Hellenic Shooting Federation. Konstantinos Myrotis, a physical education teacher, and the department's first team official, Anargyros Kapetanakis, organised competitive air pistol and air rifle shooting.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Swimming training begins at the Katerini pool
paragraphs: Following local press announcements in May, swimming training began at Katerini's National Sports Centre pool on 1 June 1981. The late Konstantinos Papadopoulos served as the first team official and Apostolos Pipilis as the first coach, establishing a programme that taught generations of children to swim.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Sokratis Skoufas receives a national handball call-up
paragraphs: In July 1981, as recorded in the board minutes of 7 July, Archelaos player Sokratis Skoufas was invited to an evaluation and training session with Greece's national handball set-up. The club record identifies him as its first handball international and a forerunner of later national-team players from Katerini.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The men's volleyball team contests promotion to the top division
paragraphs: After a strong campaign in the Second National Division, the Archelaos men's volleyball team reached the promotion play-offs in 1981. Under coach Ilias Ieroklis, the team competed for a place in Greece's top national division.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: A decade of national artistic gymnastics titles
paragraphs: Under federal coach Apostolos Samalis and team official Emmanouil Zaras, five gymnasts—Charilaos Kakalis, Konstantinos Zaras, Alexandros Katsikakis, Evangelos Chrysopoulos and Ioannis Charisis—won successive national team titles from 1981 to 1991, moving through the boys', juniors' and men's age groups.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: A water polo team is formed
paragraphs: In 1982, Archelaos formed a water polo team at Katerini's municipal swimming pool. Its junior side was formally honoured by the board on 19 January 1985, while the water polo department became active again in 1995.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Vasiliki Lazaridou contributes to administrative continuity
paragraphs: In 1983, Vasiliki Lazaridou, daughter of Theofilos, joined the club as a permanent employee and special secretary. Her many years administering the offices, athlete registers and everyday operations helped provide continuity across successive boards and sporting departments.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The handball team reaches the top national division
paragraphs: During the 1983–84 season, Archelaos's men's handball team achieved promotion to Greece's First National Division for the first time, only six years after its initial formation. The result marked the club's entry into the highest level of Greek handball.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: A youth handball title and a national cup final
paragraphs: The year 1984 was a landmark for Archelaos handball: its junior team won the Greek Junior Championship for the first time, while the men's team reached its first Greek Cup final, losing 18–24 to VAO.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Remembering president Dimitrios Giannaros
paragraphs: President Dimitrios (Mitsos) Giannaros died unexpectedly while in office on 31 July 1985. Archelaos dedicated the twelfth Dia Games to his memory and established an annual Dimitrios Giannaros award to recognise outstanding athletes.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Kostas Koukodimos sets a national youth long-jump record
paragraphs: On 21 September 1985, at the twelfth Dia Games in Katerini, 16-year-old long jumper Kostas Koukodimos reached 7.40 metres under coach Ioannis Papargyriou. The performance broke the Greek boys' national record and marked an important early milestone in his international career.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Efstatios Zannas becomes club president
paragraphs: On 23 August 1985, after Giannaros's death, physical education teacher Efstathios Zannas was elected president, with Dimitrios Papadimitriou as vice president and Christos Eleftheroudis as general secretary. His tenure, 1985–1989, included the club's 30th anniversary and the foundations of the Dios Road race.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The Papadopouleia swimming meet is established
paragraphs: After the death of swimming department official Konstantinos Papadopoulos in November 1985, the club introduced the annual Papadopouleia interclub swimming meeting in his memory in 1986. The event continued for a number of years at Katerini's National Sports Centre pool.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The Dios Dromos endurance race connects Dion and Katerini
paragraphs: In 1987, Archelaos launched the Dios Road, a 15.5-kilometre road race from the ancient theatre at Dion to Katerini's Eleftherias Square. A ceremonial lighting of the flame at Dion symbolically linked the ancient Macedonian athletic tradition with the modern city.
The museum chronology also notes a Balkan record by shooter Georgios Ioannidis in 1989.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Alexios Poulikidis wins European junior wrestling bronze
paragraphs: In 1988, Archelaos wrestler Alexios Poulikidis won bronze at a European junior wrestling championship in Izmir, competing in the 115-kilogram class. He also placed sixth at the European Junior Championships in West Germany in 1989, according to the club's wrestling archive.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Dimitrios Papadimitriou assumes the presidency
paragraphs: On 9 December 1989, following Efstathios Zannas's departure to take up duties with the national sports administration in Athens, Dimitrios Papadimitriou became president and was re-elected in 1991. His 1989–1993 tenure included the club's first men's handball Greek Cup and recognition by the Ministry of Culture.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Archelaos wins the Greek men's handball cup
paragraphs: On Saturday 2 June 1990, at the Mets indoor arena in Athens, Archelaos beat A.S.E. Doukas 27–21 (half-time 15–8) under coach Dimitris Skoufas to lift its first men's Greek Handball Cup. Leading scorers included Dionysis Anagnostopoulos (nine goals), Lefteris Eleftheriadis (five) and Giorgos Varmazis (four).
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The handball team makes its European debut
paragraphs: As Greek Handball Cup winners in 1990, Archelaos represented Katerini and Greece in European club competition for the first time. In the 1990–91 Cup Winners' Cup, the club faced Turkey's Halkbank Ankara.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Nikos Zamanis earns a silver medal in wrestling
paragraphs: In the summer of 1990, Archelaos wrestler Nikolaos Zamanis took silver in the 81-kilogram class at a world junior wrestling event in Israel. The club account records wins against opponents from Bulgaria, Russia, Korea, Romania, France, Austria and Norway; Zamanis went on to win Mediterranean gold in 1993.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Katerini hosts the Balkan Youth Handball Games
paragraphs: From 21 to 25 August 1991, Archelaos and Katerini hosted the thirteenth Balkan Youth Handball Games at the National Sports Centre's indoor arena. Vasileios Efkarpidis chaired the organising committee, and the event was regarded as an organisational success.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Kostas Koukodimos competes at the Barcelona Olympics
paragraphs: At the 1992 Barcelona Olympic Games, Archelaos long jumper Kostas Koukodimos finished sixth in the Olympic final. His earlier achievements included Mediterranean Games gold in 1991 with 8.26 metres; in 1994 he set a Greek senior record of 8.36 metres.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: A silver placing at the European Schools Athletics Championships
paragraphs: In 1992, a school athletics team from Katerini's Fourth General Lyceum, entirely composed of Archelaos athletes—K. Vasiliadis, Ath. Vlangas, K. Diamantopoulos, G. Karatzoulas, Ant. Keskines and I. Trygonis—finished second at a European School Athletics Championship in France under coach Takis Paraskevopoulos.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Christos Eleftheroudis begins his presidency
paragraphs: On 27 February 1993, Christos Eleftheroudis was elected club president, beginning an 18-year tenure spanning eight consecutive elections until August 2011. Board Minutes 70 of 14 July 1993 record Ioannis Athanasiou as general secretary of the 15-member board.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The archery department is officially founded
paragraphs: Following initial discussions in December 1991, Archelaos formally established its archery department in late 1993 as an offshoot of the shooting department, led by Konstantinos Myrotis and Anargyros Kapetanakis. Its first official competition was in November 1993; the first interclub archery games in Katerini followed in November 1994.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: A first European handball victory against RK Umag
paragraphs: On 3 October 1993, in the European Cup Winners' Cup, Archelaos defeated Croatia's RK Umag 21–19 in the return match at Thessaloniki's Neapoli sports hall. Press reports also describe the team's difficult preparation on a concrete tennis court after the Katerini indoor arena had been closed for repairs.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Archelaos wins its second Greek men's handball cup
paragraphs: In spring 1994, coached by Sokratis Skoufas, Archelaos beat Ionikos Neas Filadelfeias 27–25 at Thessaloniki's Mikra arena to win its second men's Greek Handball Cup. The team became known as the 'cup winners without a home', because Katerini's indoor hall remained closed for roof repairs for 19 months.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Greek handball runners-up and European matches against Borec Titov Veles
paragraphs: In the 1994–95 season, Archelaos finished second in Greece's top men's handball division. According to the supplied anniversary record, the club also defeated Borec Titov Veles 22–18 in Katerini on 15 October 1994 before facing Fotex Veszprém in the European Cup Winners' Cup.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The girls' basketball team places third nationally
paragraphs: In 1995–96, Archelaos's girls' basketball team, coached by Kyriakos Kanalis, finished third at the Greek national championship finals in Tripoli. The team beat Aris Thivon 65–58 and Sporting Athens 55–52 after extra time to secure bronze.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Archelaos helps found the Greek archery federation
paragraphs: Following archery's separation from the national shooting federation in March 1999, Archelaos was a founding member of the Hellenic Archery Federation on 22 May 1999. Club official Iordanis Tsachouridis was elected special secretary on the federation's inaugural board.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Shooter Maria Faka participates in the Athens Olympics
paragraphs: Archelaos shooter Maria Faka, who had set Greek junior and senior air-rifle records, represented Greece at the 2004 Athens Olympic Games in the women's air rifle event. The archival account lists her marks as 388/400 in Budapest in 1996 and 395/400 in the women's category; she later served as a club coach.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: The basketball merger forms Pierikos Archelaos
paragraphs: On 4 June 2008, Archelaos's general assembly approved the merger of its basketball department with that of S.F.K. Pierikos. The new club, S.F.K. Pierikos Archelaos, represented Katerini in the national basketball leagues, including the Second National Division in 2008–09.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: A new presidency, handball resurgence and the revival of Dia Games
paragraphs: Theodoros Diamantopoulos became president on 31 August 2011. In 2013, former international players Savvas Karypidis, Dimitris Dimitroulias and Giorgos Mastorogiannis returned under Sokratis Skoufas, helping the handball side return to the top division; the Dia en Olympo athletics meeting was also revived on 28 May 2016, with 200 athletes from 30 clubs. On 20 November 2014, during Theodoros Diamantopoulos’s presidency, the club offices moved to the First Municipal Sports Centre (A΄ DAK) in premises provided by the Municipality of Katerini.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Recent archery titles and a world junior wrestling distinction
paragraphs: During 2024–2026, the archery team won national team titles, while wrestler Dimitris Soulis took world U17 silver at 71 kilograms in Athens in 2025.
moments.source: G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis — Anniversary historical record of 70 moments (1956–2026), based on board archives.

moments.title: Seventy years of Archelaos: 1956–2026
paragraphs: In 2026 Archelaos celebrated 70 years in Greek sport. Following the death of president Alkinoos Tasopoulos on 30 July, Panagiotis Diamantopoulos was unanimously elected on 8 September. In October, the Municipality of Katerini honoured the club by dedicating the commemorative medal of the 'Run for Katerini 2026' event to its history.
